caption: The drawing contains five separate architectural illustrations of ornamental cast iron railings and structures, arranged on a single page. In the top left corner, there is a rectangular sketch depicting a section of a railing with rounded arch motifs and circular ornaments, set against a background that suggests a window with grid-like panes. Adjacent to it, on the top right, is another railing section, this time featuring a semicircular radiating pattern emanating from one corner, combined with straight vertical bars set above a decorated base. The center of the composition shows two main horizontal panels: the upper one illustrates a long, continuous balcony railing in a repeating pattern of pointed Gothic arches and quatrefoils, with the lower edge highlighted in yellow and some details in green, and below it is a more detailed elevation of an altar railing with similar Gothic motifs, centrally flanked by square columns that are topped with carved elements. In the very center of the drawing, a vertical rectangular image displays the façade of a church building with a tall central spire and pointed windows, labeled as “St. Katherine Church New Orleans Louisiana.” To the left of the central panels is a text label reading “Ornamental Cast Iron St Katherine Church New Orleans Louisiana,” and to the right is another label listing: “Balcony Railing Guard Screen Railings Altar Railing St. Katherine Church Altar.” The illustrations use primarily black ink line work, with some areas of the middle and lower railings colored in naturalistic yellow, brown, and green hues. The page background is light tan, and the objects are arranged in a functional and organized composition.
title: Cast Iron Balcony Rail
